findings.reason: The protected solution is the canonical expert-interview staircase: it starts at the top-right cell, discards one row after a zero or one column after a one, and records the best feasible column. Its O(m+n) interface-call bound, O(1) state, naming, and control flow are direct and easy to defend, so no material improvement warrants a candidate.

At (row, col), a zero proves every cell to its left in that row is zero, so moving down cannot discard an answer. A one proves col is feasible while leaving only earlier columns as possible improvements, so recording col and moving left is safe. The remaining search region is always the lower-left rectangle; columns are witnessed from right to left, making the final recorded value the smallest feasible index, or -1 when no one is observed.

An independent direct-matrix oracle scanned columns from left to right. It, the protected app solution, exact immutable native Solution.leftMostColumnWithOne implementation, a separately written staircase control, and a correct row-wise binary-search control agreed on all nine visible cases and all three benchmark tiers through read-only counting interfaces.

Seed 1428 generated 5,000 source-valid row-sorted matrices totaling 7,123,070 cells. Coverage included 504 single cells, 1,057 single-row, 1,056 single-column, 2,219 tall, 2,255 wide, 526 square, 784 all-zero, 825 all-one, 830 last-column, and 2,438 varying-boundary matrices. Both staircases used at most 184 get calls and row-wise binary search at most 601; every implementation matched the oracle.

Across three real-test repetitions, the protected solution passed all nine ordinary cases, all three benchmark outputs, and scaling with extra growth exponent -0.00 through +0.02 and largest-tier ratio 1.00x through 1.04x. The independent staircase also passed. Row-wise O(m log n) binary search passed every output and stayed within the query limit but failed only scaling each time, at +0.48 through +0.49 over the +0.15 limit.

All three benchmark tiers remain hidden and performance-only, use legal square dimensions 5, 20, and 100 with positive sizes S=m+n of 10, 40, and 200 for a 20x span, and place each row's only one in the final column. The staircase needs m+1 calls while row-wise binary search reaches 601 calls at the largest tier, remains under the source's 1,000-call limit, and reliably fails only scaling; benchmark.json was not edited.

The complete Approach now derives both safe discard moves, identifies the remaining lower-left search rectangle, proves why the last recorded column is globally leftmost, and establishes the exact m+n-1 call bound of at most 199 under source constraints. It covers row-wise binary search, exhaustive access, forbidden storage access, all-zero and all-one matrices, single rows and columns, and non-square shapes.

All nine ordinary cases are visible samples or trials. The three authenticated source examples remain exact and correctly have no invented explanations. Former hidden cases are visible, and trials cover a multi-boundary staircase, both one-cell values, a tall matrix whose boundary reaches column zero late, an all-one matrix, and one wide row with a middle transition.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode interactive matrix problem 1428 and Python as the active language. The reviewed artifacts preserve binary values, row-wise non-decreasing order, dimensions from 1 through 100, zero-based interface access, the leftmost-any-row quantifier, -1 absence result, hidden storage, and the hard 1,000-get-call limit.

The protected solve.py and immutable leetcode.py bound to verified submission 2069069965 use the same dimensions call, top-right indices, answer state, staircase decisions, and return value, differing only in the required local interface equivalent and native wrapper. Both sources and submission.json remain byte-for-byte unchanged, no candidate exists, and no remote-Accepted evidence was altered or inferred.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed the row-sorted binary definition, requested zero-based column, -1 absence rule, both BinaryMatrix methods, hidden-storage and custom-test semantics, 1,000-call and anti-circumvention rules, exactly three examples without explanations, five constraints, and two hints, with no tables, images, diagrams, notes, or follow-up. source_fidelity.json binds five modular Reference files to live-content SHA-256 6c4953c1936cbc7ad024459640e918e09f654abdf52a651b780d66d4c2b02a38 and validates without errors.
